title: The Thirty-Hole Reign Ends at Palmares
title_candidates: The Thirty-Hole Reign Ends at Palmares
Two Share the Day, One Leads Alone No More
Baker Takes the Lead, Patterson Takes the Floor
theme: A long-held lead finally breaks, a personal best arrives mid-collapse, and the last-place gap turns into a chasm.
tone: tongue-in-cheek gravitas, restrained until the collapse turns farcical
opening_hook: Palmares' parkland fairways hosted TEG's first visit and immediately rewrote the leaderboard: David Mullin's 30-hole grip on the TEG 10 Trophy lead evaporated hole by hole, while Alex Baker's career-best round somehow survived a quintuple bogey of its own.

round_story.subject: Alex Baker's Stableford personal best and Gregg Williams's near-mirror gross career-best share round-of-the-day honours at Palmares
round_story.why_it_matters: Best-round-of-the-day is usually a single name; today it split down the middle, and one half of it doubled as Alex Baker's first personal best in fifteen TEG rounds while carrying a nightmare hole he somehow shrugged off.
round_story.shape: Alex Baker's round oscillated between the ridiculous and the sublime — nine points in three holes, then a quintuple bogey at the 13th — yet his 47 points stood as both his best-ever Stableford return and his best-ever gross round. Gregg Williams, playing steadier golf throughout, quietly posted the best gross score of anyone in the field and the second-best of his own 34-round career, level with Alex on points but eclipsing him on quality of strike.
headline_candidates: Two Share the Day, One a First
Alex Baker and Williams Split Honours
Personal Best Comes With a Wobble
round_story.chosen_headline: Two Share the Day, One a First
round_story.standfirst: Alex Baker's 47 points was a career best despite a quintuple bogey at the 13th, while Gregg Williams matched him on the scorecard with the tidier round of the two.

race_story.subject: David Mullin's 30-hole grip on the TEG 10 Trophy lead ends on the 6th, and the race resets to a share at the top
race_story.why_it_matters: Mullin had led the Trophy outright since the 12th hole of round one — the longest hold of the week — and its loss, followed by a closing quadruple bogey, hands the initiative to Alex Baker and Gregg Williams with one round to play.
race_story.shape: Mullin's stranglehold, unbroken for 30 holes, gave way when Alex Baker drew level at the 6th; the lead changed hands four more times through the round as Alex, Williams and Mullin himself traded places, before a run of three birdies in four holes briefly threatened a Mullin revival. It ended instead with a quadruple bogey at the 18th, and Mullin drops to third, eleven points off a share of the lead he held for three days.
race_story.standfirst: David Mullin's spell atop the TEG 10 Trophy standings, unbroken since the first round, unravelled hole by hole at Palmares.

discovered_storylines.subject: John Patterson's horror stretch through holes 11-15 buries his TEG 10 Wooden Spoon hopes deeper still
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: Patterson was already anchored to last place in the Trophy table; a run of double-figure holes and blow-ups across five holes bled 19 gross shots and stretched his gap to the next-worst player from 5 to 14.
discovered_storylines.shape: A promising start — three pars worth nine points in the first three holes — gave way entirely from the 11th, where a quintuple bogey at the short 12th was sandwiched by more of the same at the 8th, 13th, 14th and 15th. Patterson went five holes without a single Stableford point, turning a manageable Wooden Spoon gap into a rout.
headline_candidates: The Spoon Gap Turns Into a Chasm
discovered_storylines.standfirst: A five-hole stretch without a single Stableford point turned a five-point Wooden Spoon gap into a fourteen-point one.

race_state_note: The Green Jacket picture also tightened — Mullin's cushion over Jon Baker fell from 13 to 10 — while John Patterson's slide to the foot of the Wooden Spoon table is covered separately.
